stories.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include five actively exploited flaws affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, Vanderbilt REDCap, and Perforce Puppet Enterprise. These vulnerabilities represent confirmed attack vectors currently being leveraged by malicious actors in the wild.
stories.why: Active exploitation indicates these flaws are high-priority targets for attackers, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or code execution on your infrastructure.
stories.action: Review and patch Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap, and Puppet Enterprise installations immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
stories.abstract: CISA added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Perforce Puppet, CVE-2026-115731, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw allows attackers possessing a valid CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the underlying server.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables unauthorized remote code execution on infrastructure management servers, providing attackers with significant control over enterprise configuration environments.
stories.action: Patch Perforce Puppet instances immediately.

stories.title: Siemens Industrial Software Products
stories.abstract: Siemens has identified several industrial software products impacted by the critical Node2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) found in the Node.js Brotli decoder. This out-of-bounds write flaw could enable remote attackers to corrupt memory or execute arbitrary code on affected systems.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows remote code execution, posing a severe risk to industrial control environments and critical infrastructure management systems.
stories.action: Review Siemens security bulletins and update affected software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
stories.abstract: A critical heap-based buffer overflow in the OpenJDK Base64 library, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Major enterprise software providers, including Cisco, Oracle, and Atlassian, are potentially impacted by this flaw in the standard Java runtime environment.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables remote exploitation of core Java applications, posing a severe risk to enterprise infrastructure and critical business systems.
stories.action: Monitor vendor security advisories and apply patches for OpenJDK and affected Java applications immediately.

stories.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
stories.abstract: F5 released patches for NGINX open-source and Plus editions to address a critical, decade-old remote code execution vulnerability in the HTTP/2 module. Tracked as CVE-2026-123007, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected servers.
stories.why: This is a high-severity RCE in a widely deployed web server component, potentially exposing infrastructure to remote compromise.
stories.action: Update NGINX Open Source to 1.31.9 or 1.30.7, or apply the latest NGINX Plus patches.

stories.title: Scans for LiteLLM/Starlette (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710), (Mon, Nov 16th)
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning for vulnerabilities in LiteLLM and Starlette, specifically targeting endpoints associated with CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. These flaws can be chained to facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution.
stories.why: Exploitation allows attackers to gain full control over affected systems without requiring valid credentials.
stories.action: Patch LiteLLM and Starlette instances immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
stories.abstract: Threat actors compromised an official Microsoft repository account to upload malicious versions of the agent-framework package to PyPI. These tainted updates, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, are designed to exfiltrate sensitive credentials for Azure, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps from developer environments.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting developer tools allow adversaries to harvest high-privilege cloud and CI/CD credentials directly from internal engineering systems.
stories.action: Audit environments for agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 and rotate any potentially exposed cloud credentials.

stories.title: Russian APT Poses as Employee of Hacked Firm to Breach Another US Organization
Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
stories.abstract: Apache Roller contains a critical deserialization vulnerability in its XML-RPC interface, identified as CVE-2026-129448. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected servers, and active exploitation attempts have already been observed in the wild.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows full system compromise without authentication, posing a severe risk to any organization hosting instances of the Apache Roller platform.
stories.action: Update Apache Roller to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
stories.abstract: A critical memory-corruption vulnerability, CVE-2026-114938, affects OpenJDK versions 17.0.6 and later. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution on x86-64 systems utilizing AVX-512 VBMI instructions, impacting widely deployed enterprise software including Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables pre-authentication RCE on critical infrastructure and identity management platforms, posing a severe risk to internal network security.
stories.action: Update OpenJDK to the latest patched version immediately, prioritizing internet-facing applications.

stories.title: Java4Shell, NGINX2Shell and more: Why we are not at "Yellow", (Wed, Nov 18th)
stories.abstract: SANS ISC reports that despite a recent surge in critical vulnerabilities affecting Java, NGINX, and Microsoft 365, the organization has opted not to elevate its Infocon threat level to Yellow, maintaining a baseline status for the current security landscape.
stories.why: Security teams must distinguish between widespread service disruptions and active, high-impact exploitation campaigns when prioritizing incident response efforts.

stories.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
stories.abstract: Wellington IT, a technology provider for credit unions, suffered a cyberattack that compromised the personal data of members across approximately 50 institutions, primarily based in Ireland. The firm is currently investigating the scope of the unauthorized access.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises targeting financial service providers create significant downstream risks for sensitive customer data and institutional operational integrity.

stories.title: GNU security advisory (AV26-1173)
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in GNU Emacs versions prior to 31.2 allows for arbitrary code execution. The flaw stems from a bypass in the .dir-locals.el auto-mode-alist mechanism, which can be triggered when a user opens a malicious file.
stories.why: Arbitrary code execution via file opening is a critical risk for developers and system administrators who frequently handle untrusted project files.
stories.action: Update GNU Emacs to version 31.2 or later.

stories.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
stories.abstract: Japan's RIKEN research center suspended operations of the Fugaku supercomputer after discovering unauthorized access. The breach originated from a compromised status page that leaked administrative credentials, allowing attackers to attempt logins on the high-performance system.
stories.why: Compromised credentials for critical research infrastructure highlight significant risks to national scientific assets and potential intellectual property theft.

stories.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised an access key belonging to Fireworks AI, allowing them to infiltrate the Cursor extension marketplace. This breach enabled the distribution of a malicious version of the Claude Code extension, which threat actors used to exfiltrate user data and credentials.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting developer tools can lead to widespread credential theft and unauthorized access to sensitive source code environments.
stories.action: Audit your Cursor environment and rotate any credentials or API keys exposed within the IDE.

stories.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
stories.abstract: A Chinese-linked threat actor has overhauled its EggStreme malware toolkit and infrastructure to bypass detection. The group, which targets Philippine government entities, is rotating its file hashes and command-and-control domains to maintain persistence following previous security disclosures.
stories.why: State-sponsored actors are actively evolving their TTPs to evade signature-based detection, necessitating more robust behavioral monitoring for government and critical infrastructure networks.

stories.title: Oracle Corporation security advisory (AV26-1170)
stories.abstract: Oracle has released its quarterly security updates addressing numerous vulnerabilities across a wide range of products, including MySQL, JD Edwards, and various middleware and communications platforms. Administrators should review the full advisory to identify affected components within their specific environments.
stories.why: Unpatched Oracle software is a frequent target for exploitation, potentially leading to unauthorized access, data breaches, or complete system compromise.
stories.action: Review the Oracle Critical Patch Update advisory and apply relevant patches to all affected systems.

stories.title: Dorsett Controls InfoScan
stories.abstract: Dorsett Controls InfoScan versions 1.45.0 and earlier contain multiple critical vulnerabilities, including hard-coded cryptographic keys, improper authentication, and sensitive information exposure. These flaws could allow attackers to intercept communications, steal credentials, or gain unauthorized access to water and wastewater infrastructure systems.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities pose a significant risk to critical infrastructure, potentially allowing remote attackers to compromise operational technology environments and sensitive system data.
stories.action: Update Dorsett Controls InfoScan to a version beyond 1.45.0.

stories.title: British hackers face prison for GTA 6 data breach and crypto thefts
stories.abstract: Two British individuals have been convicted for their roles in high-profile cyberattacks against Rockstar Games, the developer of Grand Theft Auto, as well as various cryptocurrency thefts. The pair now awaits sentencing for these significant digital intrusions.
stories.why: This case highlights the legal consequences for large-scale corporate data breaches and the ongoing intersection of gaming industry targeting and financial cybercrime.

stories.title: British Scattered Spider hacker sentenced to 6 years in prison
stories.abstract: The final member of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group, Tyler Robert Buchanan, received a six-year prison sentence in the United States. He was convicted for his role in a conspiracy that targeted numerous corporations and resulted in the theft of millions in cryptocurrency.
stories.why: This concludes a major prosecution against a prominent threat actor group known for sophisticated social engineering and large-scale corporate breaches.

stories.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
stories.abstract: Major financial institutions, including Citi, are restricting the use of third-party AI agents for personal finance management. These banks are clarifying that customers who utilize these automated tools assume full liability for any resulting security breaches or unauthorized account access.
stories.why: This shift in policy highlights the growing tension between consumer convenience and institutional security, potentially leaving users unprotected against AI-driven fraud.

stories.title: AttackIQ Research Reveals How Iranian Cyber Groups Hand Off Network Access to Enable Destructive Attacks
stories.abstract: Security researchers have mapped the operational patterns of twenty Iranian state-sponsored groups. The analysis highlights a collaborative ecosystem where initial access brokers, espionage units, and disruptive ransomware actors coordinate to facilitate complex, multi-stage cyber campaigns against targeted networks.
stories.why: Understanding these hand-off tactics helps defenders identify lateral movement and cross-group collaboration patterns indicative of state-backed intrusion attempts.

stories.title: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro
stories.abstract: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro contains vulnerabilities in its MCP Server involving unrestricted IP binding and cross-site request forgery. These flaws could allow remote attackers to execute unauthorized commands, access sensitive data, or compromise the underlying system.
stories.why: Exploitation could lead to unauthorized remote system access or data exfiltration within environments utilizing Mendix Studio Pro.
stories.action: Update Mendix Studio Pro to version 11.16.0 or 11.12.7.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | Can AI Do Novel Security Research? Meet the HTTP Terminator
Black Hat USA 2026 | LANJack: Turning Ads into IoT Recon Tools
stories.abstract: Researchers identified LANJack, a sophisticated attack framework leveraging programmatic advertising to conduct internal network reconnaissance. By utilizing DNS rebinding within a browser, the campaign maps local subnets and fingerprints IoT devices without requiring user interaction or suspicious clicks.
stories.why: This demonstrates a significant supply chain risk where trusted ad networks are weaponized to bypass perimeter defenses and map internal infrastructure.

stories.title: Siemens SIMATIC
stories.abstract: Siemens disclosed two critical vulnerabilities affecting various SIMATIC products. One flaw allows authentication bypass and remote code execution via session hijacking, while the other enables arbitrary code execution when opening malicious files in the WinCC Graphics Designer.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities pose significant risks to industrial control environments, potentially allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access or execute code on critical infrastructure systems.
stories.action: Review Siemens security advisories and implement recommended mitigations until patches are available.

stories.title: Siemens meta-iot2050
stories.abstract: Siemens meta-iot2050 firmware versions 01.03.01 and later contain a command injection vulnerability within the update utility. By tampering with specific configuration files, an unauthorized actor could execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges on the affected industrial IoT hardware.
stories.why: This flaw allows full system compromise of critical infrastructure hardware via privilege escalation, posing a significant risk to operational technology environments.
stories.action: Monitor Siemens for official firmware patches and implement recommended configuration mitigations immediately.

stories.title: How to Tell If It’s a Cyberattack or Just an Outage
stories.abstract: Recent widespread service disruptions across critical infrastructure have fueled speculation regarding cyber warfare. Analysts emphasize that most large-scale outages stem from technical errors, configuration mistakes, or software bugs rather than malicious state-sponsored or criminal hacking campaigns.
stories.why: Distinguishing between technical failure and active exploitation is critical for incident response teams to avoid misallocating resources during high-pressure outages.

stories.title: Siemens .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API
stories.abstract: Siemens patched two vulnerabilities in its .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API. The flaws involve path traversal and the exposure of sensitive information through error messages, potentially allowing unauthorized file writes or data leakage.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact industrial control system interfaces, potentially enabling attackers to manipulate files or gain insights into sensitive system configurations.
stories.action: Update the .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API to version 3.3.62 or later.

stories.title: Siemens Simcenter Femap
stories.abstract: Siemens Simcenter Femap versions prior to 2606.0002 contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability. By processing malicious X_T files, an attacker could trigger an application crash or achieve arbitrary code execution on the host system.
stories.why: Arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities in engineering software pose significant risks to intellectual property and operational integrity within critical manufacturing environments.
stories.action: Update Simcenter Femap to version 2606.0002 or later.

stories.title: Siemens ROS#
stories.abstract: Siemens ROS# versions prior to 2.3.1 are susceptible to a code injection vulnerability. By supplying a maliciously crafted message definition file, an attacker can execute arbitrary code within the generated program due to improper input sanitization.
stories.why: This flaw allows remote code execution in industrial software environments, posing a significant risk to the integrity of automated manufacturing systems.
stories.action: Update Siemens ROS# to version 2.3.1 or later.

stories.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
stories.abstract: A double free vulnerability in FortiOS, affecting Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices, allows authenticated local attackers to crash the newcli daemon by executing specific CLI commands.
stories.why: Exploitation results in a denial-of-service condition for critical industrial network infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Fortigate NGFW to version 7.6.9 or later.

stories.title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
stories.abstract: A new generative AI-powered platform called Artex is lowering the barrier to entry for cybercriminals. The tool enables inexperienced actors to automate vulnerability scanning and execute complex attacks by simply inputting natural language prompts into an integrated chatbot interface.
stories.why: The democratization of exploit development through AI tools significantly increases the volume and velocity of automated attacks against vulnerable infrastructure.

stories.title: Zyxel security advisory (AV26-1167)
stories.abstract: Zyxel has identified out-of-bounds write and post-authentication command injection vulnerabilities affecting several DX3300, DX3301, and EX3301 series CPE and fiber devices. These flaws exist in firmware versions 5.50(ABVY.8.3)C0 and earlier.
stories.why: Exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands or cause memory corruption on network edge devices.
stories.action: Check Zyxel's advisory for firmware updates and apply patches to affected devices immediately.

stories.title: France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack
stories.abstract: U.S. intelligence officials have issued a low-confidence assessment attributing recent cyberattacks against French infrastructure to Iranian actors. The findings remain preliminary, and investigators have not yet linked the activity to specific state-sponsored groups or organizations within the country.
stories.why: Attribution of state-sponsored cyber activity is critical for assessing geopolitical risk and potential escalation in regional digital conflicts.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Wednesday, November 18th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10184, (Wed, Nov 18th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for November 18, 2026, provides a daily summary of current cybersecurity threats and operational security updates for practitioners.
stories.why: Provides timely situational awareness regarding active exploitation trends and emerging vulnerabilities that may impact enterprise security posture.

stories.title: Atlassian security advisory (AV26-1166)
stories.abstract: Atlassian has released security updates addressing vulnerabilities across its product suite, including Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye/Crucible, Jira, and Jira Service Management. Administrators should review the specific version requirements to ensure their deployments are patched against these identified flaws.
stories.why: Unpatched Atlassian enterprise software is a frequent target for exploitation, potentially leading to unauthorized access or remote code execution within internal networks.
stories.action: Update Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye/Crucible, Jira, and Jira Service Management to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: AI Pentesting Checklist for Web Apps: 15 Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Vendor
stories.abstract: As exploitation timelines shrink, organizations are increasingly turning to AI-driven penetration testing tools. However, these vendors vary significantly in capability, particularly regarding authenticated session testing, comprehensive attack surface coverage, and the safety of production environment assessments.
stories.why: Selecting inadequate automated testing tools leaves critical vulnerabilities exposed during the widening gap between initial exploitation and official patch availability.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
stories.abstract: CISA added a critical command injection vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-114713, stems from improper delimiter handling and is currently being leveraged by threat actors in active attacks.
stories.why: Active exploitation of server-level command injection flaws poses a high risk of unauthorized remote code execution and full system compromise.
stories.action: Update UnrealIRCd to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Quality Isn’t The Main Worry About AI Pentesting — Data Privacy and Production Safety Are
stories.abstract: Automated AI-driven penetration testing is gaining traction as a solution to keep pace with rapid software development cycles. These tools aim to identify vulnerabilities faster, countering the shrinking window between software release and active exploitation by malicious actors.
stories.why: Automated testing helps security teams scale coverage to match the velocity of modern CI/CD pipelines and increasingly sophisticated automated attack vectors.

stories.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to Elon Musk deepfake scam
stories.abstract: Coinbase intercepted $4.7 million in fraudulent cryptocurrency transactions linked to a deepfake campaign. Scammers utilized AI-generated footage of Elon Musk during a high-traffic Tesla livestream to deceive viewers into participating in a fake giveaway scheme.
stories.why: Sophisticated deepfake attacks are successfully targeting large audiences, demonstrating the growing risk of AI-driven social engineering in financial fraud.

stories.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised the Optimizely platform to inject malicious code into nearly 200 major websites. By exploiting the third-party service, threat actors successfully delivered data-stealing malware to visitors of high-profile domains, highlighting the risks associated with unvetted third-party content integration.
stories.why: This incident demonstrates how supply chain attacks on common marketing and testing tools can bypass traditional perimeter security and compromise trusted web traffic.

stories.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked threat actor Cold Relic is utilizing compromised Google Workspace credentials to facilitate lateral movement and subsequent breaches of secondary organizations. Mandiant researchers identified this pattern, where initial cloud environment access serves as a staging ground for broader, multi-stage espionage campaigns.
stories.why: This highlights the danger of supply chain trust and the necessity of securing cloud identities to prevent cascading organizational compromises.

stories.title: F5 Warns 6 Critical BIG-IP Flaws Can Crash Traffic in Specific Setups, May Allow RCE
stories.abstract: F5 disclosed six critical vulnerabilities in BIG-IP systems that could allow unauthenticated attackers to crash the Traffic Management Microkernel. Exploitation requires specific configurations involving particular iRule commands or Access Policy Manager setups, resulting in service disruption until the kernel restarts.
stories.why: These flaws enable remote denial-of-service attacks against critical network infrastructure, potentially impacting availability for organizations relying on BIG-IP for traffic management.
stories.action: Review F5 security advisories and apply available patches or configuration mitigations to affected BIG-IP instances.

stories.title: Borrowed Code, Real Consequences: What OPTIMJACK Teaches Us
stories.abstract: The OPTIMJACK incident illustrates how attackers exploit third-party scripts to compromise websites. By injecting malicious code into legitimate vendor resources, threat actors can gain unauthorized access to user data, underscoring the inherent risks of relying on external supply chain dependencies.
stories.why: It highlights the critical need for robust content security policies and strict segmentation to mitigate risks from compromised third-party scripts.

stories.title: A phishing page interested in MX records, (Tue, Nov 17th)
stories.abstract: A phishing campaign masquerading as a standard credential theft attempt is specifically targeting MX records. By analyzing these seemingly generic lures, researchers discovered the attackers are harvesting domain configuration details rather than just user passwords.
stories.why: Attackers are gathering technical infrastructure data to facilitate more sophisticated follow-up attacks, such as domain hijacking or targeted business email compromise.

stories.title: An AI Debt Collection Service Exposed 6.6 Million Accounts and 315,000 Call Recordings
stories.abstract: The CreditNirvana debt collection platform suffered from critical security flaws that left millions of user accounts and hundreds of thousands of sensitive call recordings exposed. The breach potentially granted unauthorized access to private credit reports, email correspondence, and text messages.
stories.why: Exposed PII and financial records in automated debt collection systems create significant risks for identity theft and targeted extortion campaigns.

stories.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
stories.abstract: State-sponsored actors are targeting government entities in Asia and Africa using two novel backdoors, GitDoor and GraphDoor. These tools abuse legitimate GitHub and SharePoint infrastructure to facilitate covert command-and-control communications, allowing attackers to blend malicious traffic with standard cloud service activity.
stories.why: Attackers are increasingly using trusted enterprise platforms for C2, making traditional network-based detection and traffic filtering significantly more difficult for security teams.

stories.title: Oracle Patches 950 Vulnerabilities With November 2026 CSPU
stories.abstract: Oracle released its November 2026 Critical Patch Update, addressing 950 security vulnerabilities across its product portfolio. This release includes fixes for 62 critical-severity bugs and over 300 flaws that allow for unauthenticated, remote exploitation.
stories.why: Large-scale patch releases for enterprise software often contain high-risk vulnerabilities that are prime targets for automated exploitation campaigns.
stories.action: Review the Oracle Critical Patch Update advisory and prioritize patching internet-facing systems.

stories.title: Why threat hunting should matter to every board
stories.abstract: The NCSC emphasizes that passive monitoring is insufficient for modern security. Organizations should adopt proactive threat hunting to identify defensive weaknesses and leverage collective intelligence to better anticipate and mitigate sophisticated adversary tactics.
stories.why: Reactive detection often misses stealthy compromises; hunting uncovers hidden threats that bypass automated security controls.
